Subject: Medicaresys - evidence for no-learning + KMS residency and subprocessor map

Hi David —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We are moving fast on vendor review and a couple of legal/compliance asks came up that we need to close before procurement will sign: 

1) A firm operational description of how Redwood ensures customer prompts/responses are not used to further train models (we called this "no-learning" in our internal notes). We need the exact runtime controls and what evidence you can provide (logs, toggles, attestation).

2) Full subprocessor inventory for the stack that touches customer PII or prompts, including downstream analytics vendors and any managed S3/backup/storage used in pipelines. If any subprocessors are outside the US, we need a plan for onshore-only routing or justification.

3) Key management — we need confirmation whether customer-managed KMS is supported and whether keys (or key material) can be stored/used only within US regions for this account. If not possible, provide the residency and transfer details.

Attached is our draft DPA redline (we'll send the formal doc via DocuSign later). Can you route this to your security and legal and come back with an evidence checklist and a short summary we can add to our vendor binder?

Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director, Vendor Risk Management
Medicaresys

From: david_kim@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 03 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Medicaresys - evidence for no-learning + KMS residency and subprocessor map

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks. Looping in Neha (Security & Compliance) and Priyom (Product Ops) to assemble an evidence pack. High-level answers up front: 

- No-learning: Redwood supports per-tenant 'learning' toggles at the serving layer. For accounts with a no-learning commitment we disable model-updates triggered by customer prompts/responses, enforce ephemeral KV caching with TTLs, and strip examples from telemetry pipelines. We can provide an operations runbook + a signed attestation that we will not retain training datasets derived from your prompts.

- Subprocessors: We'll provide a snapshot of the subprocessor inventory and a CSV export that maps vendor role -> service -> data touching prompts/PII -> region. If Medicaresys requires onshore-only processing, we can configure request routing to our US-only Dedicated pool and exclude EU/APAC subprocessors from the routing policy for this account.

- KMS: We support customer-managed keys via Cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS/GCP KMS). For Dedicated and Private deployments we can ensure keys stay in customer-chosen regions; for hosted plans we can support BYOK where keys are stored in the customer's cloud account. We'll include a KMS residency diagram and a short implementation checklist.

We'll assemble: (a) formal attestation template, (b) subprocessor CSV, (c) KMS residency diagram, (d) operational checklist for onshore routing and evidence export. Expect a pack by Tuesday EOD.

- David
David Kim
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference

Elena / team —

See attached evidence pack (summary below) and the exported subprocessor snapshot CSV. I called out items that will require minor config changes on our side vs items that are standard for Dedicated/Private customers.

Quick summary: 
- Attestation: We have a template attestation confirming that for accounts where 'no-learning' is enabled we disable model update telemetry, we never merge tenant prompts into training corpora, and we purge ephemeral logs after configured TTL. Signed attestation attached as PDF.

- Subprocessor inventory: subprocessor_inventory_snapshot_20270607.csv includes hostnames, vendor contact, service role, and which persistent stores (if any) touch prompt text. Note: our hosted control plane uses a managed analytics pipeline in us-west-2; for onshore routing we'd exclude that pipeline and route to a us-only analytics endpoint or disable analytics entirely for the account.

- KMS flow: kms_onshore_flow_v2.png shows two deployment paths: (1) Hosted w/ BYOK (keys in customer AWS account, crypto ops occur in us-east-1/us-west-2); (2) Dedicated w/ customer-managed HSM where keys never leave the customer's VPC. We included the implementation checklist and expected lead times.

- Evidence for no-training: exported operational logs showing learning_flag=false for sample tenant (redacted), TTL purge job run history, and screenshots of the toggle in the Console. We can run a small audit job for Medicaresys and provide the resulting pdf log for procurement.

Files attached: medicaresys_dpa_redline_20270602.pdf (your doc), subprocessor_inventory_snapshot_20270607.csv, kms_onshore_flow_v2.png, redwood_no_learning_attestation_20270607.pdf

Next steps I propose: 
1) Legal teams to confirm whether the attestation plus routing guarantees satisfy DPA redlines.
2) We can schedule a 30-min ops call to walk through the KMS deployment options and set timelines for Dedicated pool provisioning if needed.

-Neha

Neha / David —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the pack, this is close to what procurement needs. A few requests from legal & infosec after an initial review:

- Contracts: the DPA redline asks for an explicit clause that "no-learning" will be operationally enforced and that Redwood will provide a quarterly export proving the learning flag remained off. Can your legal team propose specific language? If not, we'll propose ours.

- Evidence: the subprocessor CSV looks good. For any vendor that still sits in EU, can you mark whether they ever receive raw prompt text, transformed prompts, or only aggregated metrics? We need that column filled for at least the top 10 vendors by access scope.

- KMS & SLA: procurement needs an SLA bullet for key-management availability and for key-rotation support. Also a confirmation that BYOK crypto ops occur in the same region as the key (no cross-region key material transit).

- Ops call: please put 3 slots for a technical call (30 min) this week — Carlos prefers mornings PST.

If you can get updated subprocessor CSV (with access-scope column), a legal suggestion for the clause, and the KMS SLA bullets by EOD Thursday we should be able to get procurement to issue a conditional PO.

Elena Ruiz
Director, Vendor Risk Management | Medicaresys
